questions.q: Why does dbatools exist, according to this lesson?
options: SSMS is a GUI built for one server at a time; dbatools automates the repetitive, multi-server DBA work a GUI was never designed to script
It exists to completely replace SSMS for all interactive administration work
It exists because T-SQL cannot be run from PowerShell in any other way
It is a paid, proprietary Microsoft product bundled with SQL Server
questions.explain: dbatools is described as free and open-source, filling the automation gap SSMS's GUI leaves, not replacing SSMS entirely.

options: Real PowerShell objects, immediately usable with cmdlets like Where-Object or foreach
Plain, unstructured text that must be parsed manually
A screenshot of the SSMS results grid
Nothing — it only executes T-SQL without returning any result
questions.explain: Because the pipeline passes real objects (Lesson 1's core distinction), Invoke-DbaQuery's results work immediately with the rest of the course's tools.

questions.q: What does the foreach example over multiple servers demonstrate?
options: Running the same Invoke-DbaQuery against many servers in a few lines, instead of opening SSMS separately for each one
That dbatools cannot run against more than one server at all
That foreach only works with dbatools cmdlets, not other PowerShell commands
A way to permanently merge three separate SQL Server instances into one
questions.explain: The fleet-wide example is the practical payoff of combining Lesson 12's foreach with dbatools.

questions.q: How does this lesson's content relate to Azure Database Administrator Lesson 63?
options: Lesson 63 covers SQL Agent-side automation (jobs running inside the server); this lesson's dbatools approach automates similar maintenance work from outside the server, via PowerShell
They cover completely unrelated topics with no connection
Lesson 63 makes this lesson's content redundant and unnecessary
dbatools is a component that ships as part of Azure Database Administrator Lesson 63's content
questions.explain: The two are framed as complementary automation approaches — one from inside SQL Server Agent, one from outside via PowerShell.

options: Install-Module -Name dbatools -Scope CurrentUser, the same way Az was installed in Lesson 14
It comes pre-installed with every version of Windows and never needs installing
It can only be installed by a domain administrator with elevated rights
It requires purchasing a license key from Microsoft before installation
questions.explain: dbatools installs the same way as Az — via Install-Module, with -Scope CurrentUser as the common choice.
